result.title: LatentLens: Rethinking Latent Interface in Multi-Agent Systems
result.summary: Latent interfaces let agents in a multi-agent system communicate through continuous representations rather than decoded text. Prior work reports performance and efficiency gains, but neither separates latent communication from the agent harness nor examines its internal components, leaving its actual contribution unclear. We propose LatentLens, a framework that decouples the latent interface at two levels: externally from the agent harness, to measure its contribution to overall performance (RQ1), and internally into realignment compatibility, information accessibility, and propagation dynamics, to identify the benefits and limitations of each (RQ2). Across seven benchmarks with Qwen3 models, adding the latent interface to the same harness does not improve and can even substantially degrade accuracy. Internally, latent representations retain some domain information, but incompatible realignment can substantially degrade performance, and repeated latent steps can amplify representation-level failures. Thus, while latent representations may preserve information, they do not necessarily ensure effective communication, which also requires compatible realignment, information accessibility, and stable propagation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LatentLens 框架，把多智能体系统中的 latent 通信接口与 agent harness 解耦，并在内部拆分为「重新对齐兼容性、信息可访问性、传播动态」三个维度，在七个基准上检验其真实贡献。
AI.relevance_reason: 结论偏负：接口本身不带来增益甚至显著掉点，latent 保留了部分领域信息却未必可被有效使用，重复 latent 步会放大表示层失败；这与本研究关心的 latent 内容是否被使用、信息坍缩与传播稳定性直接相关，其解耦评估设计可供核查「收益归属」问题。
